content: The Diabetes Control and Complications Trial (DCCT), a pivotal study in type 1 diabetes, demonstrated that maintaining intensive glycemic control, with an A1C level around 7%, significantly reduces the incidence of microvascular complications. These complications include retinopathy, neuropathy, and kidney disease, with reductions in risk ranging from 50% to 76% when compared to standard glycemic control, which corresponds to an A1C level around 9%. Subsequent follow-up studies conducted through the Epidemiology of Diabetes Interventions and Complications (EDIC) have confirmed that the benefits of intensive glycemic control persist for decades. This is true even though the differences in glycemic control between the intensive and standard treatment groups have diminished over time.
